Sport treiben — to do sport / to play sport

This is a fixed expression in German. You don't say Sport machen (informal) as often in formal contexts.

an einem Wettkampf teilnehmen — to take part in a competition. Note the separable prefix: Ich nehme an einem Wettkampf teil.

eine Niederlage kassieren — to suffer a defeat (idiomatic). Example: Johannas Team hat eine Niederlage kassiert.

Sport ist nicht immer Mord. — Sport isn't always murder (i.e., sport can be fun too).

Die Letzten werden die Ersten sein. — The last shall be first.

Meaning: Used to console someone who has lost.

–Ich habe schon wieder verloren. –Ist nicht schlimm. Du weißt doch: Die Letzten werden die Ersten sein!

German uses mehr (more) and weniger (less) to give health advice:

  • Mehr: selbst kochen, Obst essen, fettarm essen, Gemüse essen, Kohlenhydrate essen
  • Weniger: Süßigkeiten essen, Alkohol trinken, Fast Food essen

naschen = to snack / nibble on sweets. Nächstes Jahr möchte ich weniger naschen.

Gute Vorsätze für das neue Jahr — New Year's resolutions. Common pattern: Ich möchte mich gesünder ernähren. (I want to eat healthier.)

Maria ist Managerin. Ihr Job ist sehr stressig. Maria weiß, dass zu viel Stress ungesund ist. Also möchte sie ab jetzt Stress vermeiden. Sie will sich mehr erholen.

She now:

  • Goes to Yoga every evening
  • Does Entspannungsübungen
  • Sleeps more — goes to bed earlier
  • Eats weniger Fast Food
  • Cooks fettarm more often
  • Eats Süßigkeiten only ab und zu (now and then)

fit wie ein Turnschuh sein — to be fit as a fiddle (lit. 'fit like a sneaker')

Meaning: to be healthy, fit, and well-trained.

Wer fit wie ein Turnschuh sein will, muss viel trainieren.

lectureContent.content:
F and v are pronounced the same — both sound like [f].

  • Examples: Fußball, fechten, verlieren, viel, Volk, brav

W is softer and voiced — it sounds like English [v].

  • Examples: schwimmen, gewinnen, Winter, wissen

Exception — Foreign words (Fremdwörter): In loanwords, v can be pronounced as [v] (like w) when it appears at the beginning or inside the word:

  • Examples: virtuell, Version, Klavier, Pullover, Olive, Kurve, Universität, Navigation

At the end of a word, v is always pronounced as [f]:

  • Examples: Advent, definitiv, Adjektiv, Motiv, Detektiv

Tongue twister: Viel warmes Wasser fließt durch den Fluss. Durch den Fluss fließt viel warmes Wasser.

The verb lassen means to let / to have someone do something. It is used to express having others do things for you or allowing something.

PersonKonjugation
ichlasse
dulässt
er/sie/eslässt
wirlassen
ihrlasst
sie/Sielassen

Example: Ich lasse mein Auto reparieren. (I have my car repaired.)

Use these phrases to express your opinion in a conversation:

  • Ich bin dafür, dass … — I am in favor of …
  • Ich bin dagegen, dass … — I am against …
  • Ich glaube, dass … — I believe that …
  • Ich bin der Meinung, dass … — I am of the opinion that …

Example debate topic: Sport ist Mord. — Is sport really 'murder' (too exhausting)?

Sport ist Mord. — Sport is murder (i.e., sport is exhausting / too much effort).

Meaning: Used humorously to say that exercise is hard or that one doesn't enjoy it.

–Hast du Lust, morgen mit mir joggen zu gehen? –Nee, danke. Sport ist Mord!

lectureContent.sectionTitle: Louise's Story — Part 1: A Football Fan
lectureContent.content:
It's Saturday evening. Louise was at the football stadium with her best friend Nils. Her favorite team, Bayer Leverkusen, played against 1. FC Köln.

Unfortunately, Leverkusen lost 2:3. Louise is sad.

As a child, Louise played football herself — she trained three times per week, ran a lot, and scored many goals. Her team almost never lost (Ihre Mannschaft hat fast nie verloren).

lectureContent.sectionTitle: Louise's Story — Part 2: Searching for a Sport
lectureContent.content:
Now Louise no longer plays football. She believes she is too old for it. She watches sport on TV: basketball, volleyball, and tennis.

She signed up at a gym (hat sich im Fitnessstudio angemeldet) but finds it boring — just Aerobic courses and the treadmill. She always trains alone, which she doesn't like. She'd prefer a team sport.

She can't throw or catch well, so Handball and Basketball are not options. But she knows Nils goes swimming — and she can swim well too!

lectureContent.sectionTitle: Louise's Story — Part 3: Finding Her Sport
lectureContent.content:
Louise goes swimming with Nils. They swim many lanes for almost two hours. But swimming is very tiring, they can't talk while swimming, and it's not a team sport.

On the way home, Louise sees a poster: "Wir suchen neue Fußballspieler. Wir sind Frauen zwischen 30 und 50 und spielen gern Fußball."

Louise realizes: "Vielleicht bin ich doch nicht zu alt für Fußball!" She decides to go to football training next week. She's excited!

am Ball bleiben — to stay on the ball / to not give up

Meaning: to persist, to keep going, to not give up.

Auch wenn das Üben ihr manchmal wenig Spaß macht, will Louise unbedingt besser am Klavier werden. Also bleibt sie am Ball und geht trotzdem jede Woche zum Unterricht.
